subject: Acme POC: Integration plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Byrne <alex@acme.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-16T17:32:00-07:00
Subject: Acme POC: Integration plan & success criteria

Hi Alex — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we’re all aligned:

Summary of success criteria (from today):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency under 350ms for chat flows with 1K token contexts.
- Cost: token cost below your target of $0.003 per generated token for steady-state traffic.
- Functional: support streaming responses for partial UI render, and ability to call your internal tool (search API) from the assistant (tool calling).
- Quality: top-1 intent accuracy >= 90% on the evaluation set you shared.

Proposed evaluation plan & ownership:
- Evaluation dataset: Acme will provide 300 representative prompt/response pairs and 3 integration test cases (search + conversation). (Owner: Alex)
- Integration scope: SDK-based integration on web service + streaming over SSE or WebSocket; server-side tool-calling via Redwood function calls to your search API. (Owner: Marissa + Monica for onboarding)
- Timelines: kickoff next week (week of 3/22), 2-week integration + smoke tests, 1-week evaluation run. Target pilot end-date: 2026-04-08.

Immediate next steps:
1) I’ve attached the Redwood POC template and a short tech requirements spreadsheet — please fill gaps and return by EOD Friday 3/19. (attachments: redwood-poc-template.pdf, acme-technical-requirements.xlsx)
2) Confirm who on your infra team will pair with our engineers for the streaming setup.
3) We’ll schedule a 60-minute kickoff to walk integration details and confirm success metrics.

Notes on integration specifics (high level):
- SDKs: Use our Node and Python SDKs for server-side calls. We recommend server-side host for token security.
- API routes: /v1/chat for standard chat, /v1/stream for SSE streaming, /v1/embeddings for retrieval vectors.
- Streaming: supports chunked SSE; client can render partial tokens as they arrive.
- Tool calling: Redwood can route tool calls to your HTTP endpoint via our secure webhook. We’ll provide a sample tool schema and retry/backoff behavior.

I’ll follow up with a proposed calendar invite for kickoff. Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment stubs: redwood-poc-template.pdf (4 pages), acme-technical-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Acme POC: Integration plan & success criteria — integration details

Alex — answers inline and a more concrete integration plan below.

Streaming transport: our /v1/stream supports SSE out of the box; WebSocket is supported via our lightweight proxy for customers that need WS. We’ll configure whichever you prefer during kickoff.

Tool calling & mTLS: we support webhook delivery with mutual-TLS. For the pilot we can use short-lived client certs; engineering will coordinate cert exchange.

Concrete integration plan (owners + steps):
1) Kickoff (60m) — scope mapping, confirm success criteria, finalize timelines. Owner: Marissa (schedule) — propose Tue 2026-03-23 at 10:00 PST.
2) Environment prep (2 days) — exchange API keys, certs, and sample dataset. Owner: Acme infra + Monica (Redwood).
3) SDK integration (3-5 days) — install Node/Python SDK on your backend, implement /v1/stream or WS proxy, implement tool-calling handler to forward calls to your search endpoint. Owner: Acme engineers + Monica.
4) Smoke tests (2 days) — run smoke tests using provided evaluation cases. Owner: Acme + Redwood QA.
5) Evaluation run (7 days) — collect metrics, quality signals, latency/cost reporting. Owner: Acme + Marissa to monitor.

Artifacts we’ll provide:
- Sample SDK integration repo and a minimal streaming example.
- Tool schema template and example webhook handler.
- Post-POC metrics dashboard (token usage, p95 latency, quality regression summary).

Next steps (action items):
- Alex: confirm kickoff time or propose alternatives (target: Tue/Wed AM PST).
- Alex: share 300 eval cases + the three search scenarios by 3/19.
- Monica: I’ll flag engineering availability for pairing.
- Rishi: if you can share the trial credit MOU, we’ll get procurement looped in.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

Best,
Marissa
